Young Man Builds Insane Chevy C10 Truck in His Driveway: V8 Punch and 600 Horsepower
21 photos
Photo: Autotopia LA | YouTube
Roman is 25, and he has spent the past few years working on his 1971 Chevrolet C10 right in his driveway and then racing it. The street-legal, ferocious autocross machine now hits the streets and the track, pushed forward by a completely rebuilt V8 engine, with the force of 600 horsepower.
Roman is less than half the age of his street and track companion that he rebuilt from the ground up. He did most part of the job right in his driveway, not a shop, not a garage , with no lift at hand, just jacks that made enough room for him to get underneath and work. He is definitely an old soul who treasures retro styling as much as he loves autocross.
It looks like, after 55 years on and off the road, the Chevy C10 finally got in the right hands. Those of a young man who knows exactly what it can do with a bit of a power bump. Or more than a bit. The first owner of the C10 was a farm truck guy who used it as a workhorse. The second owner bought it for his son. Roman bought it from him and slowly but surely turned it into a race truck.
He built it with purpose. Everything has a function, it’s not all show and no go. It’s got no AC, but comfort wasn't exactly a top priority for him. Instead, fun was. Loud was. Performance was. He didn't build it to take it to car shows and brag about it. He built it to take it to the track and win.
Photo: 1971 Chevrolet C10 A fully built 383-cubic-inch small-block V8 sits under the hood. Roman retained the original engine block. He originally planned to swap it for a 440, but changed his mind and just rebuilt the 383 and made it run on high-octane 101 race gas. A Tremec TKX five-speed transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels.
From farm workhorse to track machine Now it makes over 600 horsepower and 600 pound-feet of torque. A Black Widow exhaust , coming out through the side, roars out the drama of the V8 from under the hood. The power plant was outfitted with a high-performance FiTech EFI setup, which Roman credits for providing razor-sharp throttle response and reliable drivability whether he's cruising on the highway or carving corners at the track.
He is still considering an upgrade to the suspension , currently featuring Viking Performance components, but he has to come up with the right setup. A specialized Nine Lives Racing frame-mounted rear wing showed up at the back to add crucial downforce over the rear tires. A McLeod clutch helps him when he wants to smoke the tires. He was after fun and wanted a truck that he could beat on. He doesn’t want to have to baby the truck.
Photo: 1971 Chevrolet C10 The truck is sitting on a Currie 9-inch, which serves as the bulletproof backbone of this build. It effortlessly absorbs aggressive downshifts, hard clutch drops, and heavy corner-exit acceleration without flexing or breaking a sweat under track conditions. Roman relocated the fuel tank to the back for improved weight distribution.
Roman runs a high-performance Wilwood disc brake setup to safely and consistently slow his good, old 1971 Chevrolet C10 down during high-speed autocross runs or whenever he wants to show off on the highway.
Less is more when you're after fun The cabin is simple and focused on performance, because sometimes, less is more. The driver and passenger sit in RaceQuip fixed-back racing seats. It is not exactly the most comfortable sitting choice, but Roman chose them for the enhanced racing feel that he gets on board. He never wanted to build a lounge on wheels. Those seats make perfect sense in a truck that spends more time at the track than it does on the road.
The driver holds a Cannonball Performance steering wheel and gets all the relevant driving data on the aftermarket digital and LED Intellitronix gauge cluster, with a classic yet sporty appearance. That is what the truck's creator wanted in the first place.
Photo: 1971 Chevrolet C10 Roman retained the original door panels, along with the door hinges and window cranks, but came up with a Level 7 pedal assembly. Roman made efforts to keep the truck looking as vintage as possible so that he would not alter its DNA.
On the road, the driveway-built Chevy C10 is stiff, light, and bad-mannered when you step on it. It can smoke tires until tomorrow (and until it runs out of rubber, of course), and it can make other motorists scratch their heads in surprise at the stoplight.
Looking all beat-up and run-down, nobody would expect it to launch like a rocket. Roman hasn't fixed the paint imperfections and isn’t planning to do it. Told you he's an old soul and patina works for him.

source_document.body:
Volkswagen is offering its Chinese-market Jetta M6 electric sedan with nearly 290 miles of CLTC-rated range for less than $12,000 (USD), and if that’s not what “der people’s wagen” should be all about, I don’t know what is.
Launched as a joint venture between FAW and Volkswagen Group, the Jetta brand’s first battery electric car is finally here – and it is a genuinely accessible , capable , and kinda decent-looking family sedan in the same way VW’s original Type I was when it was first developed in the 1940s.
The new Jetta M6 was launched earlier this in three variants: the 465 Pro, 555 Max and 555 Ultra; each priced at 79,800 yuan (~$11,800), 89,800 yuan and 99,800 yuan, respectively, with the model numbers corresponding to the car’s estimated CLTC range in kilometers (which maths out around ~285 and 345 miles, if you’re curious).
Built on FAW’s Jiesi architecture , the M6 measures 4,806 mm long and 1,868 mm wide, putting it right in that sedan sweet spot between the Civic/Corolla and Accord/Camry crews, and within a few mm this way and that of the Tesla Model 3, so it should have plenty of room for young professionals and families – but the M6′ real selling point is its tech.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
High tech, low cost
Jetta M6 interior.
Inside, the Jetta M6 offers an 8.88″ driver display along with a big 15.6″ central touchscreen that integrates Chinese AI assistants Doubao and DeepSeek and ships with Apple CarPlay baked in. Advanced ADAS with , “intelligent cruise assistance, automatic emergency braking, and automated parking” is standard.
The entry-level “465 Pro” version of the Jetta M6 comes equipped with 42.9 kWh LFP battery and a 113 kW (~150 hp) electric motor driving the front wheels, a combination the company says is good for a 8.3-second sprint to 100 km/h (62 mph). Stepping up to the 555 versions gets you a larger 51.9 kWh battery and more powerful 145 kW (~195 hp) motor that cuts that sprint to 6.8 seconds.
Both the 42.9 and 51.0 kWh batteries are lithium iron phosphate deals supplied by CALB, with charging from 20% to 80% taking about 30 minutes.
Mass market model
Jetta M6 555 Ultra.
Would those features and performance numbers be enough to get you to look at something like this in the US, even at twice the price? It seems to me that North America’s VW dealers need all the help they can get, and a volume leader like this with a “back to basics” ad campaign that plays on a different kind of nostalgia – nostalgia for a time when people could afford a Jetta , maybe? – could be a winner. Let us know what you think in the comments.

18FT Travel Trailer Works Some Serious Magic to Fit Everything Onboard
11 photos
Photo: Aguiar Trailers
The economy might be taking a turn for the worse but don't expect that to put a damper on wanderlust. If anything, it could further drive sales in the RV sector, as people will be looking for alternatives to pricey vacations and accommodation.
If that turns out to be the case, smaller will probably be better again. After years of offering more of everything, which has resulted in larger RV solutions of all kinds, manufacturers are already showing signs of preparing for downsizing, scaling down their existing models or introducing new ones.
This one isn't, because it's actually been doing "small" since it was founded in 2013. Aguiar Trailers is a Brazilian company specializing in fiberglass towables that break the mold in design and functionality, if not construction.
Their flagship model, called Coruja 3.0, is a perfect example of that. It's actually the model that sits at the foundation of all the others in the company's catalog, and a single look at it will tell you why. Coruja 3.0 does just about everything differently and, in the process, offers lots of functionality and a high degree of comfort for three people in standard configuration.
Photo: Aguiar Trailers That's nothing to scoff at, especially if you consider its dimensions.
This single-axle travel trailer comes in at just 5.5 meters/18 feet of total length (it's 3.2 meters/10.5 feet long in the body), 2 meters/6.5 feet of width, and 2.5 meters/8.2 feet of height. It's very compact, yet it offers sleeping for three or even four if you add an optional bunk bed, a nice galley kitchen, a wet bathroom, and actual space to move around.
To boot, it features a private balcony shielded from the elements, which is the highlight of the floorplan.
Photo: Aguiar Trailers The Coruja 3.0 starts with an imported AL-KO chassis on top of which Aguiar Trailers builds a fiberglass body with an obvious teardrop-style inspiration. Some components are imported along with the chassis, like the windows, but the rest is built in-house. Aguiar takes pride in building a local product that, sadly for everyone else, is available only locally.
The highlight of the floorplan is a split rear door opening in the manner of a tailgate on gas-assisted struts and a drop-down patio. In nice weather and in the absence of critters, it's the perfect way to bring the outdoors inside as you lounge in the dinette, on the adjoining sofa, or throw together a quick meal in the kitchen.
This private "balcony" also allows Coruja 3.0 to offer two separate entryways, with the other being the traditional campsite side entry. Still, Aguiar finds a way to change things up here as well, turning what would otherwise be "dead space" as you enter into the shower space.
Photo: Aguiar Trailers Indeed, you enter into and through the bathroom. It's not even immediately apparent because Aguiar hides the toilet, the shower wand, and the flip-down sink behind a door. To use the shower or the toilet, you simply swivel that door to close off the room from the rest of the space, and you get a decent amount of space to work with.
Also here, you get a Komeko gas water heater and a cassette toilet. Unlike what you'd find in similarly sized trailers, no, you don't have to sit on the toilet to shower; you have plenty of space for that in the entryway.
At the very rear of the trailer is the kitchen. Somewhat hilariously, a flip-down section of the counter that extends available workspace drops into the shower space, blocking the entryway in the process. Aguiar believes that dead spaces shouldn't exist onboard such compact RVs, and you can tell from the way they're making the most of them.
Photo: Aguiar Trailers The kitchen is equipped with a two-burner gas cooktop, a small under-the-counter 12V fridge, and a stainless steel sink with a cover. Like with the majority of fiberglass towables, storage space is limited inside the Coruja 3.0 as well.
Across the way is a long bench that doubles as a single bed at night, taking up occupancy to three. The other two will be sleeping at the front, where the U-shaped dinette converts into a bed by dropping the table. A fourth person, preferably a child, can sleep in a bunk Aguiar adds over the dinette as a request, but that costs more than just money: it also costs you the storage options overhead.
The owners of the latest completed unit, shown below, did not want a bunk bed. Instead, they got storage on either side and framing the standard 9,000-BTU AC unit.
Photo: Aguiar Trailers The Coruja 3.0 comes standard with AL-KO stabilizers , a manual step, a storage box on the tongue, marine plywood floor, marine plywood cabinetry with fiberglass, an 115Ah leisure battery, a 20A charger, a 600W inverter, and LED lights. Two tanks of 100 liters (26.4 gallons) each carry fresh and wastewater.
Options include exterior colors and decals, a choice of interior finishes and colors, and extra features like a 24-inch TV on a swivel mount, induction cooktop, and a side awning. You can also choose to upgrade existing features: a bigger battery to which you can add a choice of solar panels, or bigger wheels.
Photo: Aguiar Trailers The Coruja 3.0 starts at R$129,990, which is approximately $26,200 at the current exchange rate and irrelevant to readers outside of Brazil because Aguiar Trailers doesn't export their products. But window shopping is always a cheap option to have, so make the most of it with the video tour below.

New BMW M350 xDrive Gets a Virtual Tuning Job, Do You Dig the Sportier Design?
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design
BMW has an entirely new 3 Series in its portfolio, the G50. The model debuted almost one month ago, and has yet to hit the assembly line, as the production is scheduled to commence in 2027 at the Dingolfing factory in Germany.
Therefore, we can say that the paint has barely dried on its body, yet it seems that a good chunk of the tuning world (and not only) already wants a piece of the action. That’s understandable, given that the petrolhead crowd has big expectations from this model, and while you are reading these lines, chances are your favorite tuner is already deciding what to cook up for the sports sedan in order to make it cool.
I would have said “more cool” instead of “cool,” but in my opinion, there is nothing “cool” about the new-generation BMW 3 Series . Well, other than the platform, because it is based on an updated version of the old CLAR architecture. This means that despite venturing into the Neue Klasse era both inside and out, it still shares its nuts and bolts not only with its predecessor, the G2X, but also the G3X 5 Series, the G32 6 Series, G01 X3, G02 X4, G2X 4 Series, the usual M models, the demised Z4, and the Toyota GR Supra.
So, why is it not cool in my vision? Because the Neue Klasse design does not do justice to this otherwise iconic model. The vizor-like face makes it look like a mainstream model, perhaps one made by a Chinese brand, and the back end is definitely on the quirky side of things, too. And then comes the interior, with its tech-filled nature, which will likely age like a smartphone to the point where not many gearheads would want a used G5X 3er a few years from now.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design The same will also apply to its range-topping sibling, the new-gen BMW M3 , which is reportedly due in 2028, some one year after the mechanically-unrelated M3 Electric launches. The ICE M3 will feature some M Concept Neue Klasse-inspired design cues, a similar interior with the usual M touches, a dedicated chassis setup, uprated brakes, and a 3.0-liter twin-turbo straight-six, likely with MHEV assistance, that could offer north of 600 hp.
Meanwhile, if you want a fast new-gen 3er, then you will have to settle for the new BMW M350 xDrive. And it is this exact model that has recently fallen into the hands of the rendering crowd, as a small chunk of its has imagined what this thing would look like if it were visited by the tuning fairy. The same goes for @a.c.g_design on Instagram, which signed the digital illustrations shared in the gallery above, and would want to know what you think of it.
This virtually-tuned BMW M350 xDrive features a new hood, a tweaked bumper at the front with an apron attached to it, side skirt extensions, and dedicated trim on the front fenders. Out back, it is home to a new diffuser with an extra brake light in the middle, close to the OEM bumper, a double bubble-like ducktail spoiler, and a wing. The Y-spoke concave wheels with their silver finish are new, the car rides closer to the ground, and features a blue look on the outside, complete with some black elements, and tinted windows all around.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design Quite strangely, there are no yellow daytime running lights on deck, and in case you forgot, these will be a thing for this version of the new-generation BMW 3 Series. The M350 xDrive has 437 bhp to play with, which equals 325 kilowatts and 443 metric horsepower, and the 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged straight-six engine with 48-volt mild-hybrid assistance develops 428 pound-feet (580 Nm) of torque, the model’s spec sheet reveals.
Channeling the output and thrust to the rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system is an eight-speed automatic transmission. BMW’s new M350 xDrive takes 3.9 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, which makes it 0.2 seconds faster than the current M3 Sedan, aka the base one. The M3 Competition Sedan, which has a bit more oomph (503 instead of 473 brake horsepower), hits 60 mph in 3.8 seconds, and the M3 Competition xDrive Sedan, with its 523 bhp, will complete the sprint in 3.4 seconds.
Ordering the new BMW M350 xDrive with sport tires means that this model will eventually run out of breath at 155 mph (250 kph), and the top speed is 130 mph (210 kph) without this option. And we cannot wait to see how fast the next-generation BMW M3 is, and how much power it has, though it is logical to assume that it will offer more than 600 hp in order to be on par with Audi Sport’s new RS 5 and Mercedes-AMG’s C 63.
Now, what’s your take on this virtually-tuned new-gen BMW 3 Series ? Is the CGI makeover a yay or a nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Λutomotive Custom Garage (@a.c.g_design)

Mitsubishi Galant VR-4 Turbo Wants an ICE Piece of the Popular Toyota Camry Hybrid Sedan – Rendering
9 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
Mitsubishi Motors North America, Inc. (MMNA) reported earlier this month its third-quarter sales for the US automotive market, and the company reached a mere 18,543 deliveries, down from 19,647 last year.
MMNA also revealed its year-to-date performance, which was less than impressive: 68,554 units versus 73,400 during the first nine months of 2025! Once again, all we can say is that MMNA is currently a shadow of a shadow of its former self, unfortunately. Luckily, there are hopes.
That’s because the Japanese automaker has set in motion MMNA's five-year business plan – "Momentum 2030" – in the United States, and it covers “the brand's mid-term intentions for product and business transformation.” More precisely, Mitsubishi wants to bring to market in the US one new or completely refreshed model each year until 2030, seeking to renew and expand its family.
Currently, it sells the Outlander and Outlander Plug-In Hybrid plus the Outlander Sport, as well as the Eclipse Cross. While the small and affordable Mirage has been discontinued, the company recently introduced the Nissan Leaf-based 2027 Mitsubishi Eclipse Sportback electric vehicle , and the updated business strategy now also includes the option to launch a rugged, off-road-focused Outlander variant in the first quarter of 2027 along with a mid-size pickup truck built in partnership with Nissan.
Will that be enough? Well, at least someone thinks it’s not. That person is also a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators, and he stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to do something for Mitsubishi.
Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a reborn Mitsubishi. More precisely, he says he was “curious if the new Eclipse Sportback’s grille would look good on a sedan.” Thus, he proceeded to help Mitsubishi’s lineup with a new passenger car.
Meet the reborn Mitsubishi Galant VR-4 Turbo, a reenactment of the automobile nameplate produced by Mitsubishi from 1969 until 2012 in its regular Galant form. There have been nine generations of the model that started as a compact car but then evolved into mid-size attire starting in 1983, and the sixth through eighth iterations also had a flagship VR-4 (Viscous Realtime 4WD) version. The latter was produced from 1987 through 2002, originally intended for homologation for the new Group A of the World Rally Championship, though it was quickly discontinued in favor of the iconic Lancer Evolution.
Now the pixel master has decided to bring it back with the quirky ‘fat-lipped’ look of the Eclipse Sportback EV , though as far as we can tell we’re now dealing with an ICE model, given the added Turbo moniker. As such, it could easily pick a fight with the AWD version of the 2027 Toyota Camry hybrid, right? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)

Is This a Suitable Look for the Mighty BMW M8 Coupe?
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozportt
BMW’s new-age lineup, especially the Neue Klasse models , makes me miss the older cars from back in the day, when cars used to be on the more appealing side of things, and the emissions regulations weren’t this strict.
If you had asked me about the E60 BMW 5 Series / M5 a few years ago, I would have told you that it should be put to death by fire. However, this model has aged like fine wine, and so has the entire 5er family, for that matter, save for the latest G9X. The latter is the new generation, and in case you haven’t heard, the Munich-based company is turning it into a Neue Klasse model for the mid-cycle refresh.
For what it’s worth, I do not hate the latest 5er and M5 that much anymore, but that is probably because of the realistic renderings that have previewed their Neue Klasse successor. And deep down, I want to look back at these rides a few years from now and say that they have aged very nicely. Time has its own way of fixing everything, and fingers crossed that it will manage to fix these rides, as well as the new 3er, X5, and so on.
But there is a quite modern Bimmer that has also aged greatly, and it does not get much credit online these days anymore. We are talking about the 8 Series, which recently left the assembly line for good. It was offered as a two-door coupe, the G15, a two-door convertible, the G14, and a four-door sedan (Gran Coupe), the G16, joined by a very cool Alpina B8, and the range-topping M8.
Photo: Instagram | revozportt The latter was also offered in all three body styles, and just like the lesser 8 Series , it built on the same familiar CLAR construction. This is also the foundation stone of the old 7 Series flagship sedan, the previous-generation X5, the current X6 and X7, and the XM, which remains a BMW M standalone product, and still hasn’t one any beauty pageants.
BMW ceased production of the M8 one year ago, though that does not make it any less exciting. In fact, it still looks fantastic, this writer thinks, and even though it is officially dead and buried, certain tuners still continue to drop images of various modded projects based on this model. One of the latest is RevoZport, which recently took to its social media channels to release the pictures shared in the gallery above.
This BMW M8 Coupe wears “a complete street kit,” according to the tuner, and this is what RevoZport had to say about this build. The car features a very sharp-looking apron attached to the front bumper, a new hood, new side skirt extensions, a three-fin diffuser with cutouts on each side for the quad exhaust tips, a ducktail spoiler, and a few other add-ons at the front and rear that can be seen in these pics.
The wheels appear to have come from the aftermarket world, too, and that’s hardly a surprise, given that no modern-day tuning job would be complete without a fresh set of alloys. These are concave, feature a Y-spoke design, and have a silver look. Speaking of the colors, the exterior of this BMW M8 Coupe is teal, and that has probably been obtained via wrapping it. The extras have a dry carbon look and some minty touches on them.
Photo: Instagram | revozportt This part would normally be dedicated to the interior, but since the pictured BMW M8 Coupe is all about the so-called “street kit,” we cannot see the cockpit. Well, not entirely, anyway, but zooming in on certain images reveals that the cabin is mostly black, from what we cannot see, and we reckon it hasn’t been touched with the tuning stick.
We can probably say the same about the powertrain, and in case you forgot, the car came with the S63 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8. The engine was good for 600 ps (591 hp/441 kW) and 750 Nm (553 lb-ft) of torque. The M8 needed just 3.3 seconds to hit 100 kph (62 mph) from a standstill, and the M8 Competition, with its 625 ps (617 hp/460 kW) and the same thrust as the non-Competition model, was one-tenth of a second faster.
Alpina’s B8 used the N63 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8, rated at 620 ps (612 hp/456 kW) and 800 Nm (590 lb-ft) of torque, and was just as fast as the regular M8 from 0 to 100 kph, as the sprint was completed in 3.3 seconds.
Now, you already know how I feel about the BMW M8 (and 8 Series), as I definitely love it, but the tuned example is not exactly my cup of tea, and that’s probably due to the wacky color choice. But how do you feel about this one? Is it a yay or a nay in your book? View this post on Instagram A post shared by RevoZport (@revozportt)

Husband Surprises Wife With a 1992 Chevy Blazer Like They Had When They Started Dating
16 photos
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube
Left for dead, baking under sunlight, this 1992 Chevrolet Blazer looks like it is on the verge of being eaten by grime and mold. However, its owner wants to surprise his wife with a vehicle similar to the one they used to travel across the country when they were high school sweethearts, and calls the detailer to clean it up.
Tyler bought the 1992 Chevrolet S10 Blazer to surprise his wife. But the moment it was delivered to his home, he realized it would surely be a surprise. A very dirty one. He couldn't give his missus something to work on, so he called a detailer, trying to turn a run-down, beat-up SUV into the vehicle she has always dreamed of.
They had one just like it when they started dating, back in 2016. But the SUV started falling apart at some point, and nostalgia made her dream of another square body. Tyler kept an eye on the market, trying to fulfill her dream, and now the time has come to make it come true.
Getting the Blazer cleaned up is not just about surprising his wife, but also bringing back good old memories from the times they were at the beginning of their relationship, when they used to travel carelessly all across the country.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube Now that they have two daughters, free time has significantly shrunk, and she has never asked for much. But the Blazer is a dream car for her. " Without her, nothing I do would be possible ," he honestly admits about the lady who was his high school sweetheart and is now his wife and the mother of his children. Isabella has just turned four, and Payton is only seven months old.
But cleaning it won’t exactly be a walk in the park. A thick layer of green mold covers every single inch of the hood, roof, and badges, while the cabin is covered in dust and grime, and rust has bitten big chunks out of the wheel wells and sills.
Tyler has big plans for it: bring its shine back and shoe it with new OEM wheels and new tires. He has already found a set of original wheels that Chevrolet sold with the Blazer back in the 1990s. He is well aware that he hates the wheels that are currently on this vehicle.
However, the detailer cleans the wheels fitted on the vehicle because Tyler is planning to sell them. He also unscrews the guard from the hood because it will no longer be needed. RJ of WD Detailing uses the pre-wash, an alkaline cleaner, to remove as much dirt as possible and get rid of the heavy organic contamination embedded in the clear coat.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube He does a quick spot test before the actual procedure, and the pre-wash does melt the unwanted layer of dirt. But first things first: RJ needs to blow the debris off the vehicle first, using compressed air, to avoid getting the whole studio dirty.
Pressure washing reveals the actual color of the Blazer , a beige that was hard to guess under the grime. A whole ecosystem has been created on the roof of the vehicle after years of neglect, so he has to work hard on that area as well.
Then, RJ uses a citrus degreaser to get rid of all the dirt that has gathered around the fuel cap before pressure washing it, too. Covering the whole Blazer in a thick layer of soap is the next step of the cleaning mission. The iron kryptonite will help the detailing team get rid of the iron particulates collected over the years.
The cabin, even though it seems to be in good condition, is covered in grime. The interior of the S10 has never been a luxury lounge on wheels, but it has always been durable and functional. But hard plastics and basic amenities don't make it less functional. On the contrary.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube RJ removes the seats to have enough room to clean the carpet and floor mats. Vacuuming, blowing the dirt off with compressed air, and using the drill brush to lift the deep-seated mold already work miracles. Then, the stain extractor makes it look almost brand-new.
The hard plastics might be unpleasant to touch, but they are extremely durable. Once the layer of sticky dirt is removed, the door panels, center console, and dashboard prove that they stood the test of time.
A 4.3-liter V6 engine powers the 1992 Chevy Blazer. Referred to as the "Vortec 4300," the 4.3-liter V6 is essentially a legendary 5.7-liter Chevy 350 small-block V8 with two cylinders chopped off. GM used the same pistons, rods, and valve train components to keep production costs low.
When it did run, it pushed out 160 horsepower (162 metric horsepower) and 230 pound-feet (312 Newton meters) of torque. The two-door four-wheel-drive version with a manual transmission, like this SUV right here, accelerated from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 9.6 seconds on its way to a top speed of 101 mph (167 kph).
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube But all these are a thing of the past, and the top speed of the Blazer is that of the trailer that carries it around. The engine bay is baked in grease and dust, so the detailers have to scrub all that dirt off so that they can give Adam, the mechanic, a clean workspace.
He is the right man for the job. His first five vehicles were all S10 Blazers. The first surprise is that the oil looks clean, so he is confident that he can already try to see if it cranks over. But the V6, as reliable as it is known to be, is also very stubborn and completely dead.
Adam decides to drop the original fuel tank, which has most likely been the victim of rust, with the help of RJ’s donkey kick, and bolt in a brand-new tank. He figures out that the Blazer has a faulty distributor, so out goes the old one and in goes a new one. That final replacement is enough to get the engine fire up.
However, it is a short-lived glory, because the engine dies back again. Adam has to replace the injectors. That swap seems to be the silver bullet, because the V6 cranks back to life.
Riding on new wheels with new tires, the 1992 Chevy Blazer drives onto the trailer on its own power. Detailers take it back home. They and Tyler have a surprise in store.

This Citroen Relay Is a Swamper-Style Camper Van With a Cozy Oak Interior
22 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed
Lately, I've been looking at more swamper-style vehicles, and I fell in love with the look. Today, I have a swamper camper van that blends a cool exterior look with much-needed creature comforts. What makes this project even more impressive is the fact that it's a DIY creation.
"What's a swamper?" you might be wondering. It's an off-road-inspired conversion of a standard passenger or panel vehicle. It's built to look like a tough overland vehicle – some even act like it, although most just have the looks.
What we have here is a conversion based on a Citroen Relay with a long wheelbase and a high roof. It was created by a man known online on YouTube as "Van life deployed."
As usual, let's start the tour with the exterior. This Relay is certainly an eye-catcher due to its unique look. First off, it's finished in black and white – the lower rocker panels, the bumper, part of the roof, and the hood are black. The rest of the van minus some mods is white. What's more, the van rides on Extreme Alloy wheels wrapped in Comforser CF110 all-terrain tires.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed At the rear, you'll discover a ladder that offers quick and easy access to the roof. There, the builder installed a roof rack holding two 175 W solar panels, a two-in-one antenna (for TV and Wi-Fi), and a Fiamma F80S awning measuring 3.7 meters (12 feet) in length. It also offers plenty of free space to add other accessories or gear.
Other notable mods include side steps, four windows (two on each side), and power and water connections.
Slide the door open, and you'll be greeted by a beautifully built interior. It really feels like a tiny studio apartment, especially since it has a closed layout and you can't see the cabin. By closed layout, I mean that there's a wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice a variety of oak elements including oak slat walls and oak cabinetry, grey laminated cabinet faces, grey carpeted flooring, and a white ceiling.
The divider wall I mentioned earlier integrates a tiny window and an overhead storage unit with a spacious headliner shelf, a shelf with a lip, and a small cabinet.
Next to the same wall, the builders added one of the two kitchen units. It offers a dual-burner induction stovetop, a bit of surface area for meal prepping, three drawers, and a cabinet.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed Straight ahead as you enter, you'll come across the bathroom. It boasts a shower with a handheld wand, two wall niches for storage, a Trelino composting toilet, and an overhead cabinet with a mirror. What's more, a Maxxair Dome vent fan draws out moisture and nasty smells, while a retractable door prevents any water from splashing outside.
The other part of the kitchen is on the same side as the bathroom, further inside the camper. It has a deep black stainless steel sink, a 95-liter fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, two outlets, and a wall spice rack. There's also a cabinet underneath the sink that houses a water filtration system.
On the opposite side, you'll discover an overhead cabinet, a tea shelf, and a counter with a top. The counter hides the rig's power system – its highlights are a 300 Ah lithium iron phosphate battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed You can use three charging sources: shore power, solar power , and DC-DC charging while the engine is running. Basically, it offers all you need to be able to travel off-grid without worries – you just have to make sure you have enough water, food, and fuel.
Next to the overhead cabinet I mentioned above, you'll find an inverter controller and a battery monitor.
The rear part of the living space is reserved for seating and sleeping. The day setup consists of two benches and a table in between. This area sits a bit higher than the rest of the interior, and the extra height was put to good use thanks to a floor compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed Two cabinets and an overhead shelf above form a "U" shape and offer additional storage space. The benches have hinged tops that can be lifted to reveal more room. However, the driver-side bench also houses the freshwater tank and a Truma Combi heater that heats both air and water.
You'll also notice charging points, two reading lights, and a TV attached to a wall-mounted swivel. A nice and clever touch is that the van's converter added an Alexa system and connected it to the RGB lights in the back of the van, so you can control them by using voice commands.
Creating the sleeping arrangement is easier than you'd think. You must drop the table to the same height as the benches to connect them, add extra panels to fulfill the same purpose as the dropped table, and rearrange the cushions.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Van life deployed As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 100-liter (26-gallon) freshwater tank and a 55-liter (14.5-gallon) under-mounted greywater tank with a drain tap.
All in all, this guy created a well-equipped home on wheels that efficiently uses the little interior real estate available, all hidden behind a cool swamper-style exterior.
He ended up selling the van, but he shared that a similar spec could cost around £45,000 to £55,000 ($59,585 to $72,826) depending on mileage and vehicle specs, as well as how greedy the builders are.

1966 Dodge Hemi Coronet Fails to Sell Despite Low Mileage and Matching Numbers
15 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
In late September, I told you about a cool 1966 Dodge Coronet 500 that was scheduled to go under the hammer at Dallas/Fort Worth 2026. It's a rare Hemi Mopar, and I was expecting it to change hands without issues. Well, the hammer just dropped, and the Coronet failed to find a new home.
The gavel dropped at $75,000, which is far below the usual auction price for a vehicle in this condition. The owner also set a reserve, which was obviously higher than the top bid. The Coronet 500 was thus driven off the stage with a "bid goes on" status.
In Mecum talk, this means that the company will attempt to sell the car behind closed doors. It usually talks to bidders who may be willing to pay more or accept offers from other potential buyers. But "bid goes on" lots rarely change hands this way. It's more likely that we will see this Hemi Coronet at an upcoming auction.
The Mopar's inability to find a new owner is surprising. That's mainly because Hemi-powered classics are quite rare. Chrysler debuted the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) V8 in 1966 and kept it in production through 1971. However, it only sold nearly 10,000 units. This figure is for all model years and nameplates combined.
If we break it down, we get vehicles with hundreds and even tens of examples sold each year (some even have one-digit figures). When it comes to the 1966 Coronet, Dodge delivered only 700 units that year. That's out of a total of around 250,000 examples, so we're looking at a production of under 1%.
Of the 700 examples made, only 340 were ordered as range-topping 500-badged models. And of these, only 136 were hardtops equipped with the three-speed TorqueFlight automatic transmission. Needless to say, not all of these cars survived, and, moreover, even fewer still have their numbers-matching drivetrains.
Yes, this Mopar still relies on the original Hemi engine and automatic gearbox. Both were likely rebuilt, as the engine bay looks squeaky clean (but still factory correct). In fact, the entire car appears to be in pristine condition, and the black vinyl interior is described as original.
The ad states that the vehicle received one respray in the original Citron Gold Metallic, which likely means that this classic is a semi-survivor. We're looking at a vehicle that spent a lot of time in storage and was given a refresh at some point. The low 25,913-mile (41,703-km) reading on the odometer confirms this scenario.
How much is this Mopar actually worth? That's hard to say without a proper inspection, but Hemi-powered classics in this condition tend to sell for six-figure sums nowadays. But in this case, it's probably well under $150,000.
While this rare Hemi failed to sell, a Six-Pack-powered 1969 Dodge Super Bee crossed the block for a whopping $151,250 at the same event. The A12-powered Mopar also has a numbers-matching V8 engine, and it's one of 826 units equipped with a four-speed manual gearbox.

McLaren 720S Gets Digitally Nuked With a 1,000-HP ZZ632 Chevy V8, Becomes the 'Big Block Supercar'
9 photos
Photo: wnvld / Instagram
Just like any other good old exotic automaker, McLaren has its ways to keep interest at an all-time high among the one percenter. But we bet they didn’t think of this virtual solution…
Just recently, we heard that McLaren will sell five of its historic Formula One cars because it wants them back on the track to be raced, rather than stored, and the options include anything from the 1991 MP4/6As to Lando Norris’ 2023 MCL37A. They also announced that the McLaren 750S will soon come to an official end, sometime in 2027, after almost a decade of continued V8 supercar performance, basically making the last units a collector’s item and increasing their value exponentially.
Also, not long ago, the company changed its logo to create a refreshed branding identity that will trickle down from the McLaren McL 6GT limited-production analog-style supercar introduced during the summer at the 2026 Monterey Car Week to all of its upcoming production models. Last but not least, more novelties may be coming, as the brand recently filed for new Remuera and Muriwai trademarks that echo Bruce McLaren’s New Zealand roots.
But what if people still can’t come to terms with the disappearance of the McLaren 720S lineage – the model that is now known as the 750S ? Well, no worries, as nothing will be forgotten, at least not if you’re a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
For example, Andreas Wennevold, the virtual artist behind the ' wnvld ' account on social media, has a knack for American muscle in vintage-modern form, as it turns out, and he recently asked himself what would happen if you put the 1,000-horsepower Chevrolet Performance ZZ632/1000 , the largest and most powerful crate engine ever built by General Motors, into a McLaren.
The naturally aspirated 632 cubic-inch (10.4-liter) V8 big-block produces 1,004 horsepower and 876 lb-ft of torque while running on basic, standard 93-octane pump gas, and the pixel master was basically inspired by the “early M8 racecars that used Chevy engines; I thought it would be fun to do a modern version.” He’s talking about the McLaren M8 series, which used massive Chevrolet big-block V8 engines that also acted as a stressed structural chassis member, featuring 7.0-liter 427-cubic-inch V8s in 1968 and then graduating to 8.1-liter V8 options later on.
Now, the modern reinterpretation of a “supercar with GT3 handling and the rowdiest N/A sound” is a McLaren 720S featured in two distinct color schemes: a matte black and exposed carbon fiber version with subtle orange elements, as well as an all-out orange and carbon fiber variant, which acts as a direct CGI reference to the original racecars.
